items.question: By what alternative penalties can the offender's purification be achieved instead of execution?
premises: A fine of wealth can serve as a corrective penalty.
Bodily chastisement can serve as an alternative corrective penalty.
These penalties are presented as means of purification for the offender.
items.inference: The offender may be purified through a monetary fine or through bodily chastisement rather than by being killed.
uncertainties: The exact scope and severity implied by kāya-damena are not specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: His purification is accomplished either by a fine of wealth or by bodily chastisement.
